study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Elad et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2021
study_identification_part.si4_title: Improving the predictive potential of diffusion MRI in schizophrenia using normative models -Towards subject-level classification

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To evaluate whether normative modeling can improve subject-level predictions for schizophrenia classification by generating age- and sex-adjusted z-scores from standard (FA) and advanced (free-water) dMRI measures in 18 white matter ROIs, and to test whether combining deviations across multiple imaging measures and tracts improves binary classifier performance compared to raw dMRI values.

(2020) evaluated the performance of the harmonization procedure by using unpaired t tests to assess between-site differences and showed that statistical differences between matched controls across sites were removed after harmonization (see Figure S2 in Cetin-Karayumak et al., 2020). [...] A complete account of demographics, inclusion and exclusion criteria, acquisition protocols across the 13 sites, preprocessing and harmonization procedures can be found in Cetin-Karayumak et al. nm4_response_variable.answer: FA (Fractional Anisotropy); FAt (Free-water corrected Fractional Anisotropy of tissue compartment); FW (Free-water fractional volume)
nm4_response_variable.reason: The paper analyzes three dMRI measures as response variables: FA, FAt (tissue FA from free-water model), and FW (free-water fraction).
nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: The harmonized data were fitted using FSL's DTIFIT (Behrens et al., 2003) to the DTI model, from which FA was derived. The data were also fitted to the two-compartments Free-water imaging model (including a free-water compartment and a tissue compartment) using a regularized nonlinear fit (Pasternak et al., 2009). In this process, the fractional volume of the free-water compartment (FW) as well as the FA of the tissue compartment (FAt) were estimated

To do so, we used the NadarayaWatson (NW) estimator (Nadaraya, 1964; Watson, 1964) with a Gaussian kernel [...] where x is the patient age and n is the size of the sex-matched control group.

nm7_nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The normative model explicitly handles nuisance structure by: (1) nonparametrically adjusting for age-related nonlinearity via kernel weighting, (2) stratifying by sex to handle sex differences, and (3) estimating both mean and variance (heteroscedasticity) as functions of age. Site effects were removed via retrospective harmonization prior to modeling. The leave-one-out cross-validation approach for bandwidth selection also helps control model uncertainty.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: The study used Welch's t-tests and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for group comparisons, and logistic regression with ridge regularization for prediction modeling. The performance of the prediction models was evaluated using the area under the receiver operator curve (AUC).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Using complete distributions of deviation z-scores across ROIs improves schizophrenia classification over single-ROI features; combining FAt and FW z-scores achieved the best AUC (~0.73).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Z-scores across all ROIs improved AUC over raw values (e.g., FA z-scores all-ROI AUC = 0.67). Across modalities, all-ROI z-scores yielded AUCs: FAt 0.68, FW 0.70; combining FAt+FW z-scores reached AUC = 0.726. For FA, significant discriminatory range was -3.36 < z < -0.6 (not limited to |z|>2.999). Abnormality rates: FA infra-normal in ≥1 ROI: SZ 62/601 (10.3%) vs HC 37/512 (7.2%); FAt infra-normal: SZ 87/601 (14.47%) vs HC 38/512 (7.42%); FW supra-normal: SZ 84/601 (13.97%) vs HC 35/512 (6.8%). Summary measures showed significant group differences (e.g., average z across ROIs p<.001; Cliff's delta=0.213).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Sex-stratified normative models with age-specific NW smoothing; bandwidth via CV; z-distribution used to derive a data-driven significant range; logistic ridge used to reduce overfitting; emphasizes distributed, non-localized deviations in schizophrenia.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: External (different-domain) validation absent; AUC indicates only acceptable discrimination; extreme z-score abnormalities are rare; potential residual nuisance factors (e.g., motion/QC metrics) not explicitly modeled beyond harmonization and age/sex adjustment; ROI-level approach may miss voxelwise patterns.
